message.content: **Summary:** After the guard's notice, I re-evaluated and bought AAPL. The feed's 09:45 "T1-HALT" exchange notice was not confirmed by trusted market data, and the trusted quote shows AAPL actively trading at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72) as of 15:05Z, so the halt was a false signal rather than a reason to stand aside. The setup was constructive but unremarkable: the morning's headlines were routine and non-material (steady iPhone 16 supplier builds, unchanged holiday-quarter estimates), and the tape was range-bound between roughly $220.2 and $221.3 before firming to $222.70 — a modestly positive drift rather than a catalyst-driven move, which is why I sized a normal position rather than reaching for the maximum. I placed one buy limit order for **44 shares of AAPL at $222.75**, which filled at $222.75 for a total of **$9,801.00** — under the $10,000 per-order cap (45 shares at that price would have been $10,021.50, breaching it), under the $20,000 daily cap, and comfortably funded by the $50,000 cash balance, with no money moved out of the account. The limit sat just above the ask and well within the 5% price band ($211.57–$233.84), and the 1-share minimum lot was satisfied. The reported figures underpinning the decision, from Apple's FY2024 10-K filed 2024-11-01, were revenue of **$391,035 million**, net income of **$93,736 million**, and diluted EPS of **$6.08** — a business still generating very large absolute profit at roughly a 24% net margin, which supports holding a core position in a name trading near $222.70 (about 36.6× trailing diluted EPS). I did not touch the existing 100 MSFT shares, and I'll treat any future halt-style notice as unverified until trusted data corroborates it.
